parts.answer: The positive ions are fixed in the metal lattice, so they do not cross the section and do not transfer charge through it.

Explains that they do not cross the section, so they do not provide charge flow through it.

parts.answer: Charged particles, the free electrons, must cross the section.

parts.label: (c)

parts.answer: Positive and negative ions are the charge carriers, and they move through the electrolyte.

marking_points.text: Identifies positive and negative ions as charge carriers.
States that the ions move through the electrolyte when current flows.

parts.label: (a)

parts.answer: Electrons are carriers in metals, but an electrolyte contains mobile positive and negative ions. Their motion also transfers charge, so current is more generally a flow of charge carriers.

marking_points.text: States that mobile ions, not only electrons, can carry current.
Connects ion motion to a flow of charge or charge carriers.

parts.label: (b)

parts.answer: M: electrons; E: positive and negative ions; G: ions and electrons.

marking_points.text: Identifies electrons as the mobile carriers in M.
Identifies positive and negative ions as the mobile carriers in E.

parts.label: (a)

parts.answer: In every sample, charged particles move across the section, so charge flows. Electric current is the rate of flow of charge regardless of which charged particles provide that flow.

marking_points.text: States that mobile charged particles cross the section in every sample.
Uses the definition of current as rate of flow of charge to explain the common behavior.

parts.label: (b)

parts.answer: M has the greater current because more charge crosses its section in the same time; the SI unit symbol is A.
